context:
Goal: a guard PR's fix check catches a defect that Haiku misses.
Problem (rule): a reviewer's model is a role rule, which needs your word.
Based on (ruling): rule agent-model-cap, where reviewers run Sonnet from round 2 on.
Departs from: main, where the fix check runs on Haiku — a moves it to Sonnet for guard and check PRs.

options.gain: A stronger read on the PRs that change what a guard lets through.
options.label: Sonnet for the fix checks of guard and check PRs (recommended)
options.lose: One Sonnet call per fix check.

options.label: Keep Haiku
options.lose: A weaker read on guard fixes.

reply: a, 14:44 CST, counted by lane guard-fix-check-sonnet. Your question: no agent split, but more than prose. Today the spawn guard refuses a reviewer above Haiku unless its brief says round 2 or 3, and a fix check carries no round. So the lane builds three parts: a fix-check marker in the brief that the guard reads (one shared constant); agents/reviewer.md line 73 and the model-per-role table row; and a merge-tool refusal of a Haiku fix check on a guard or check PR, so Sonnet is required, not only allowed. It is a guard change, so it gets full review rounds. This closes on the lane's done report.
short: Guard fix checks: Sonnet or Haiku?
title: Should the fix check on a guard or check PR run on Sonnet instead of Haiku?
why: You asked on item 279 (Nov 6) how option c made sense there: "isn't that a separate thign?". This is it, on its own.
